review_critical_caveats: The complete MacKay book gives a finite-alphabet IID typical-set treatment in Chapter 4 and ideal-real arithmetic in Chapter 6; it does not itself prove the later fixed-register coder or stationary-ergodic SMB results.

Gray author-hosted corrected Chapter 3 was read in full for this lane, but its printed SMB proof retains internal mismatches at pp. 53-57. Findings record the exact repairs: M>=3/delta, bad-prefix tail mass <=delta/6, accepted block lengths M<=ell<N, tests for starts k<L-N, and the final N-symbol boundary gaps.

The Stanford note fully proves expected LZ78 rate universality for stationary finite-alphabet sources. The separate complete Ziv-Lempel 1978 primary article proves individual-sequence compressibility relative to finite-state IL encoders; its theorem is not identified with every modern LZ78 bitstream framing.

The complete Kontoyiannis 1998 recurrence proof establishes the stationary-ergodic sliding-window LZ77 match-length limit for finite alphabets with the paper’s overlapping-reference convention. It does not prove a particular pointer/length/EOF bitstream overhead theorem.

Moffat-Neal-Witten’s printed b-bit-L arithmetic finish is used. Their minimal-bit finish is delegated to source code not obtained here, and bits_outstanding needs an explicit guard, width bound, or synchronized reset policy.
Finite-register arithmetic endpoint sums need widened or checked intermediates; the integer coder is approximate, with the paper’s loss formula and operating assumptions recorded in findings.md.
unresolved_limits: No countable-alphabet SMB theorem or finite-entropy countable-source AEP is asserted.
No LZ77 pointer/length/EOF bit-rate optimality, arbitrary-input implementation bound, or implementation complexity theorem is asserted.
No theorem is asserted for nonergodic fixed-length vanishing-error rate or adaptive arithmetic-model optimality.
Continuous-parameter MDL requires an explicit precision or density-volume convention; it is not identified with exact Bayesian evidence.

The Gray nonergodic and AMS results are recorded as source-backed statements; a scaffold proof must expose the ergodic-decomposition/stationary-mean domination steps, which are absent from current library suppliers.
